record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: In curved string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections and interacting fluids, what asymptotic behavior is produced by dominant versus subdominant curvature contributions?

evidence.quote:
3.4 Curved string cosmologies with interactions
This deals with the important case of curved universes with interacting ﬂuids in string cosmologies with higher order curvature corrections. We expect to see the eﬀects of dominant as well as subdominant curvature asymptotically.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially curved, homogeneous and isotropic FLRW string-cosmological background with metric
ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 [ dr^2/(1-kr^2) + r^2 dΩ^2 ],   k ∈ {-1, +1},
sourced by a dilaton φ(t) and N interacting perfect-fluid components with energy densities ρ_i(t), pressures p_i = w_i ρ_i, satisfying interaction-modified continuity equations
ρ̇_i + 3H(1+w_i) ρ_i = Q_i(ρ_1,…,ρ_N, H, φ, φ̇),   Σ_i Q_i = 0,
where H = ȧ/a. Let the gravitational sector be governed by the tree-level string action augmented by higher-order curvature (α'-type) corrections
S = ∫ d^4x √(-g) e^{-φ} [ R + (∇φ)^2 + λ_1 α' L_{GB} + λ_2 α'^2 L_{(R^3)} + ⋯ ] + S_matter,
where L_{GB} = R^2 - 4R_{μν}R^{μν} + R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} is the Gauss–Bonnet invariant and L_{(R^3)} denotes the next higher-curvature correction.

Question. Classify, as t → ∞ and as t → t_* (any finite-time singularity), the possible asymptotic regimes of the scale factor a(t), the Hubble rate H(t), the dilaton φ(t), and the fluid densities ρ_i(t), distinguishing the cases in which (i) the spatial-curvature term k/a^2 is asymptotically dominant over the higher-curvature corrections, (ii) the higher-curvature α'-corrections asymptotically dominate over the spatial curvature, and (iii) both contribute at the same asymptotic order. In each case, determine the resulting late-time/early-time attractors of the dynamical system and the conditions on the interaction terms Q_i and the equation-of-state parameters w_i under which each regime is realized.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this asymptotic classification problem for curved, interacting string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections was located. Related works treat either Gauss–Bonnet-coupled interacting dark fluids in flat backgrounds, or higher-curvature corrections without interacting fluids, but a complete classification combining spatial curvature, α'-corrections, and fluid interactions does not appear to be available, so the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological Solutions of Higher-Curvature String Effective Theories with Dilatons
status_evidence.snippet: Examines higher-curvature corrections (quadratic and quartic) in bosonic, heterotic and type II string effective actions; cosmological solutions exist but are affected by dilaton.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-curvature string-cosmology solutions are studied but without full curvature+interaction asymptotic classification.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic curvature corrections to stringy effective actions
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates Gauss-Bonnet higher-curvature corrections in heterotic frameworks regarding de Sitter vacua.
status_evidence.claim: Related higher-curvature analyses exist but do not resolve the asymptotic dominance question in curved interacting backgrounds.
